title: Your first open chords
summary: Em, Am, and D -- the three chords that unlock most songs.

steps.title: What is a chord?
steps.body: A chord is three or more notes played together. The most useful chords on guitar live in the first three frets and use open strings -- those are 'open chords'. We'll start with three of the most common: Em, Am, and D.

steps.title: E minor (Em)
steps.body: Press strings 5 and 4 at the 2nd fret with fingers 2 and 3. All six strings ring out. Em is one of the easiest shapes on the guitar; you only fret two notes.

steps.title: A minor (Am)
steps.body: Skip string 6 (don't strum it). Use finger 1 on string 2 fret 1, fingers 2 and 3 on strings 4 and 3 at fret 2. The same shape moved up a string is the foundation of many barre chords later on.

steps.title: D major (D)
steps.body: D is small and triangular: skip strings 6 and 5. Finger 1 on string 3 fret 2, finger 2 on string 1 fret 2, finger 3 on string 2 fret 3.

steps.title: A theory aside
steps.body: Em, Am, D are all triads -- root + 3rd + 5th. The minor chords use a flatted 3rd (3 semitones above the root); the major chord uses a regular 3rd (4 semitones). That single note is the difference between 'sad' and 'happy'. We'll explore this in 'Building major chords'.
